title: Sustainable Supply Chain Management for Homogenized Food Products and Dietary Foods in the Polish FMCG Market
content: The study sought to analyze the sustainable supply chain management of homogenized food products and dietary foods on the Polish market. All companies operating in this segment of the food industry in Poland participated in the study, which demonstrates the comprehensive nature of the research. The empirical part of the article was prepared using a survey method and the gradient technique. The research findings illustrate the current state of practices in the area of sustainable supply chain management. Based on the analysis and interpretation of the research results, it can be concluded that the initiatives undertaken by companies in the area of sustainable supply chain management are selective in nature and do not fully align with the concept of sustainable development. Measures focused on social aspects related to employees, as well as those centered on the broadly defined optimization of product deliveries—which impact delivery costs—deserve praise. A negative aspect requiring improvement is the use of transportation resources in supply chains and companies’ approach to environmental and economic aspects. The research points to the need for a more decisive and comprehensive integration of social, environmental, and economic areas, utilizing as many of the resources available to companies as possible—including financial, material, and human resources. These research findings can serve as a resource for companies that intend to distribute their products in a more sustainable manner, respecting environmental and social values, and turning this into a competitive advantage.
